propositions: BindingStore's 799-line module conflates byte persistence, lifecycle policy, recovery, and rotation—requiring extraction behind a unified facade while preserving all serialization and public-method compatibility

Three internal owner modules (repository, lifecycle, recovery) must replace monolithic BindingStore internals without changing unknown-field handling, JSON formatting, shallow all_bindings() semantics, or existing file structure
Retirement completion must check durable tombstone identity against live forward and reverse bindings; only explicit unretire revokes the tombstone intent, never automatic liveness observations
Live recovery must run after exclusive-lock staleness validation but before remote issue fetch and binding walk to prevent new liveness evidence interleaving with completion
Extracted code must preserve rotation-before-live ordering, per-file atomic replacement, selective five-file publication, and comment-identity immutability without eager rewrites or general journals

All six delivery slices and acceptance criteria must maintain byte-identical serialization, fault tolerance, identity guards, and 404-grace behavior while adding recovery atomicity and unretire semantics
